Senses.Explanation: A colloquial demonstrative: “thus,” “like this,” or “in this way.” It occurs 28,391 times in the allowlisted corpus and points to a stated situation without naming a new object. The Sixth Patriarch asks Huairang, “what thing comes thus?” (什麼物恁麼來); records also pair coming thus with going thus and say that thus, not-thus, and both together will not do. In public interviews it marks a student’s inference (恁麼則), a proposed understanding (恁麼會), the exact moment at issue (正當恁麼時), and a condition (若恁麼). A later citation doubles both sides: “thus, thus” and “not thus, not thus.” The variant spelling “thus” (與麼) is the same word. Chan makes this ordinary pointer a pervasive hinge of question and answer, but its deictic referent remains one sense.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense. Different grammatical frames and positive or negative appraisals are readings of the same demonstrative, not different things. The “if so, then” compound (恁麼則) has its own entry; link it without collapsing it into the base.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖曰。什麼物恁麼來。曰說似一物即不中。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), section on Nanyue Huairang. Huineng asks Huairang, “What thing comes in this way?” (什麼物恁麼來); Huairang supplies the following answer. The headword is Huineng's, so responsibility is assigned to him rather than to the section subject.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭曰。恁麼也不得。不恁麼也不得。恁麼不恁麼總不得。子作麼生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Yaoshan Weiyan. Shitou Xiqian (頭 = 石頭) says that in this way, not in this way, and both together will not do, then asks Yaoshan what he will do (子作麼生).

Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), section on Xinghua Cunjiang. The precentor Kebin (克賓維那) speaks the graphic variant (與麼); Xinghua then strikes him. Kebin is not yet in the roster, so his pinyin name is used provisionally.
Blue Cliff Record of Yuanwu Foguo (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin says that as soon as one understands it in this way (纔恁麼會), it has already been missed (蹉過了也).

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道。正當恁麼時如何。蟬聲時到耳。雁影忽迎眸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). In his own formal address, Yuanwu Keqin asks what it is like precisely at such a time (正當恁麼時如何), then gives the cicada-and-wild-goose lines.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若恁麼見得。便有自由分。不隨一切語言轉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Yuanwu Foguo (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin uses the demonstrative conditionally: “if it is seen in this way” (若恁麼見得).

Occurrences.Kwic: 先德道恁麼恁麼又云不恁麼不恁麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Recorded Sayings of Foyan Qingyuan. Foyan cites an unnamed former worthy doubling “in this way” and then “not in this way.” Responsibility for the citation belongs to Foyan; the earlier speaker is not named.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃呵呵大笑云。山僧恁麼說話。大似無夢說夢無事生事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄). Yuanwu Keqin laughs and calls his own speaking in this way (山僧恁麼說話) comparable to speaking of a dream without a dream and producing an affair where none exists.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以道。以大圓覺為我伽藍。身心安居平等性智。恁麼則不可以方所為限。不可以時分為拘。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄). Hongzhi Zhengjue uses the linked fixed compound (恁麼則) and continues that it cannot be limited by place or constrained by divisions of time. This anchors the compound mentioned in the note but does not count toward base-headword depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。直須恁麼。師乃云。名不得象不得。從來清淨不受染污。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄). In a public exchange, Hongzhi Zhengjue answers, “It must be in this way” (直須恁麼), then continues his address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覺上座今日也恁麼去也。還相委悉麼。天共白雲曉。水和明月秋。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄). Hongzhi Zhengjue refers to himself as Jue and says that today he too goes in this way, then asks whether the assembly understands.

Occurrences.Kwic: 要做大漢，大漢不恁麼做；要做大漢麼，須是退步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sixin Wuxin, third of the Four Huanglong Records (死心悟新禪師語錄（黃龍四家錄第三）). Sixin Wuxin says that a great fellow does not act in this way and that one who would be a great fellow must step back.
